## The gender of nouns

You have been able to notice that many words do not have the same gender in Latin as in French. The attribution of a gender to a given word may still seem to you as delicate a thing as it is arbitrary. In truth, there as on many other points, experience is the best guide. So, by dint of seeing NOUN-ADJECTIVE tandems such as ars technica, clamor magnus, etc., you will end up knowing perfectly the gender of the corresponding nouns. Thus, in these last two, ars is evidently feminine and clamor masculine.

But while waiting for all the words to become familiar to you, you can save time by learning a few rules… more or less rich in exceptions.

## 1. Gender by meaning

First of all, one can know the gender of nouns thanks to their meaning:

1° MASCULINE are the nouns that correspond to male beings or beings considered as such:

> vir, viri, *the man*; mas, maris, *the male* (diminutives, masculus and masculinus); lupus, -i, *the wolf*; agricola, -ae, *the farmer*; nauta, -ae, *the sailor* (masculine professions); aquilo, -onis, *the north wind*; Garumna, -ae, *the Garonne* (river); Montes Saxei, *the Rocky Mountains*.

For these last three, one will remember that winds, rivers and mountains were represented by male divinities. However, Alpes, -ium, f. pl., *the Alps*, is feminine.

2° FEMININE are, besides names of women (Lucia, Marcella, etc.) and the names of feminine professions (ancilla, *the servant*, etc.):

- the names of female animals (lupa, -ae, *the she-wolf*) or considered as such: aquila, -ae, *the eagle*;
- the names of trees: populus (alba), *the (white) poplar*.

3° NEUTER are the nouns or expressions to which it is truly impossible to attribute a gender, for example clauses and verbs in the infinitive: decorum est pro patria mori, *it is beautiful to die for one's country*; indeclinable words (if they do not designate persons); e.g. zero absolutum,<sup>1</sup> *absolute zero* (temperature below which it is theoretically impossible to go).

## 2. Gender by form

But one can also recognize the gender of nouns thanks to their form.

### A) 1st and 2nd declension

For the 1st and the 2nd DECLENSION, the question is simple. Nouns in -a are generally feminine, nouns in -us generally masculine, nouns in -er are always masculine, and nouns in -um are always neuter.

### B) 3rd declension

In the 3rd DECLENSION the endings are very varied:

1° As *masculine* endings we will find for example:

- -or, -oris: odor, *smell*; maeror, *grief*, etc.; but soror and uxor are feminine;<sup>2</sup>
- -os, -oris: flos, *the flower*; ros, *dew*; but os, oris, *the mouth* or *the face*, and os, ossis, *the bone*, are neuter.

2° *Feminine* endings:

- -as, -atis: dignitas, *dignity*;
- -do, -dinis: longitudo, *length*;
- -io, -ionis: motio, *movement*;
- -go, -ginis: imago, *the image*.

Exceptions: ordo, -inis, *rank* and cardo, -inis, *the hinge*, which are masculine.

Also remember that masculine words in -tor, -toris, make the feminine in -trix, -tricis: auctor, *author*, *instigator*; f. auctrix, instigatrix.

3° *Neuter* endings:

- the endings -c, -l, -n, -t: lac, lactis, *milk*; animal, animalis, *the animal*; discrimen, -inis, *danger*; caput, capitis, *the head*;
- the endings in -ar, -ur, -us (we are still in the 3rd decl.): pulvinar, -aris, *the large bed*; robur, -oris, *strength* (vigour); opus, -eris, *work, the work*;
- the ending in -e: mare, maris, *the sea*;
- words in -a of Greek origin: problema, problematis, *the problem* (in a general way, Greek words keep their gender after their Latin naturalization).

Exceptions: sal, salis, *salt*; fur, furis, *the thief*; mus, muris, *the rat*, which are all three masculine.

We could lengthen the list of typical endings of the 3rd declension, but we will not do so in order not to lengthen further the list of exceptions!

### C) 4th and 5th declension

Finally for the 4th and the 5th DECLENSION:

1° nouns in -us, -us, are masculine; e.g. appulsus, *landing*.

Exceptions: acus, *the needle*, domus, *the house*, idus (f. pl., gen. iduum), *the ides* (13th or 15th of the month); manus, *the hand*; porticus, *the portico*; tribus, *the tribe*, which are feminine;

2° nouns in -u, -us, are all neuter. Unfortunately there are very few of them: cornu, *the horn*; genu, *the knee*; veru, *the spit* or *the javelin*;

3° nouns in -es, -ei, are all feminine: fides, *faith*; res, *the thing*, etc.; except:

- dies, *the day*, which is always masculine in the plural (dies praeteriti, *past days*), and also in the singular if it means a determined day (die tricesimo primo mensis augusti, *on the 31st day of the month of August*), but quadam die, *a certain day*;
- meridies, *noon*, which is always masculine.

## Exercise

As an exercise, try to find the gender and declension of the words below. When you have finished, check against the second list, which gives for each word: the genitive (whence the declension), the gender and the translation.

> maeror – sors – contio – ars – discrimen – atomus – nucleus – pulex – dignitas – propoma.

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

| Word | Genitive | Gender | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| maeror | maeroris | m. | *sadness* |
| sors | sortis | f. | *lot* |
| contio | contionis | f. | *assembly* |
| ars | artis | f. | *art* |
| discrimen | discriminis | n. | *difficulty* |
| atomus | atomi | f. | *atom* |
| nucleus | nuclei | m. | *kernel* |
| pulex | pulicis | m. | *flea* |
| dignitas | dignitatis | f. | *dignity* |
| propoma | propomatis | n. | *aperitif* |

</details>

SECOND WAVE: the 21st lesson.

---

1. Zero is given as an indeclinable neuter by Goelzer (*Nouveau Dictionnaire Français-Latin*) and cited as such by Bacci and Badellino. Absolutus, -a, -um, is used in the sense indicated above by Soccorsi (see Bibliographical Index).
2. Arbor, arboris is feminine, like most names of trees (vid. sup. 1, 2°); aequor, -oris, *expanse of water* (sometimes of land) and marmor, -oris, *marble*, are neuter, but one will notice that these exceptions are only apparent, for the o is short in these three nouns. One will note on the same occasion cor, cordis, *the heart*, which will give us a total of three feminine and three neuter in -or.
